@jratcliff I was into Dogecoin long before Elon, and it’s always been about having fun. I agree people shouldn’t throw money at it trying to get rich, but it IS a viable currency. We sent the Jamaican bobsled team to the olympics with it in 2014!
@russian_market #dogecoin definitely! @DogecoinRise @itsALLrisky
@jratcliff All that being said, I think it’s also cheaper for me to send you $10 in $Doge vs $Btc. And for what it’s worth, I think there is an active volunteer development team.

@jratcliff I think most of the benefits of Dogecoin are psychological (because it was never meant to be a real competitor). It’s fun, it’s funny, it has a great community of positivity, has a history of giving back. Good enough reasons in my book to be a part of it.

@ConanOBrien Dogecoin is the literal underdog of crypto. Everyone hates on it but its vibrant community of positivity can’t be brought down. Its benefits are more psychological than utility; It’s fun, funny, it has a history of giving back, and people like it, what’s wrong with that?

There’s room for both coins, and I fully expect to live in a world where my Dogecoin is priced in BTC and I used it at the grocery store and Bitcoin holds my life savings, and dollars are a thing of the past. If you want to bash a shitty currency keep it focused on the USD. /rant
The feud between #bitcoin and #dogecoin is ridiculous. A rising tide lifts all ships. Pettiness only serves to create more FUD, and actually deters people who might be interested in crypto. 1/3
